task:
Build the marketing website for The Bayes Group, an AI enablement, training and consulting firm founded by two credentialed data scientists, specializing in custom AI development. React web app: Vite + React + TypeScript with react-router; plain CSS with a design-token theme (CSS custom properties); `npm run build` produces dist/index.html. Static site: no backend, no accounts, no analytics, no third-party scripts, no external font or image CDNs.

Brand and look: the name is "The Bayes Group", the tagline is "Evidence-driven AI, built for your business." It must look like a top-tier professional consulting firm: deep navy (#0B1F3A) and white with one accent color (teal #1F8A8A), generous whitespace, a serif font stack for headings and a clean sans-serif stack for body text (system fonts only), and a simple wordmark logo drawn in inline SVG (a small bell-curve mark followed by the text "The Bayes Group"). Responsive: it works on a 390px wide phone and a 1440px wide desktop, never scrolls horizontally, and on phones the header navigation collapses into a "Menu" button that opens and closes the links.

Every page has the same header (the wordmark linking to /, nav links Services, Training, About, Contact, and a "Book a consultation" button linking to /contact) and the same footer (the wordmark, the line "AI enablement, training and custom development.", the nav links, and "© 2026 The Bayes Group"). Each page sets its document title, for example "Services | The Bayes Group"; the home page title is "The Bayes Group | Evidence-driven AI". Each page has exactly one h1.

Pages:

1. Home (/): a hero with the h1 "Evidence-driven AI, built for your business.", one sentence of value proposition, and two buttons: "Book a consultation" (to /contact) and "Explore services" (to /services). Then three pillar cards: "AI Enablement", "Training" and "Custom Development", each with two or three sentences and a "Learn more" link to its section on /services (/services#enablement, /services#training, /services#custom-development). Then a "How we work" section with four numbered steps: Assess, Design, Build, Enable, each with one sentence. Then a "Why The Bayes Group" section with four points: credentialed data scientists, hands-on builders, vendor-neutral advice, and knowledge transfer so your team owns the result. It ends with a call-to-action band: "Ready to put AI to work?" and a "Book a consultation" button.

2. Services (/services): h1 "Services", then three sections with ids enablement, training and custom-development, in that order. Enablement lists: AI readiness assessment; use-case discovery and prioritization; AI strategy and roadmap; AI governance and responsible-AI policy. Training lists: executive AI briefings; hands-on team workshops; deep-learning bootcamps for technical teams; custom curricula. Custom development lists: LLM and retrieval-augmented (RAG) applications; AI agents and workflow automation; predictive models and ML pipelines; deep-learning solutions; integration with existing systems. Every item shows its name and a one-sentence description, and each section ends with a "Typical engagement" line (for example "2 to 6 weeks").

3. Training (/training): h1 "Training", then a catalog of at least six course cards. Each card shows the course title, its audience (exactly one of: Executives, Managers, Technical teams), its format (Half-day briefing, 1-day workshop or Multi-week bootcamp), its duration, and a "You will learn" list of three items. At least one course exists for each audience. Above the catalog are four filter buttons: All, Executives, Managers, Technical teams. "All" is selected at first and shows every course; choosing an audience shows only that audience's courses; the selected button is visibly marked and has aria-pressed="true".

4. About (/about): h1 "About", a mission paragraph, a "Why Bayes" paragraph (Bayesian reasoning, updating beliefs as evidence arrives, is how we approach every engagement), two founder cards with clearly marked placeholder content (name "Founder Name", role "Co-founder & Principal Data Scientist", a credentials list and a short bio, both marked as placeholders to be replaced), and four values: Evidence over hype; Build to transfer; Vendor-neutral; Responsible by design.

5. Contact (/contact): h1 "Book a consultation", the email hello@thebayesgroup.com, and a form with labelled fields Name, Email, Company, "What can we help with?" (a select with AI Enablement, Training, Custom Development, Not sure yet) and Message, plus a "Send message" button. Name, Email and Message are required, and Email must be a valid email address; on submit, each invalid field shows its error message next to it ("Please enter your name.", "Please enter a valid email address.", "Please enter a message.") and nothing is sent. A valid submit makes no network request: it shows "Thanks, we'll be in touch within one business day." and clears the form.

6. Any unknown route shows a "Page not found" page (h1 "Page not found") with a link back to the home page.

Accessibility: semantic landmarks (header, nav, main, footer), every form field has a label, keyboard focus is visible, and text meets WCAG AA contrast.
validation: npm install (.) ok, npm run build (.) ok, ui renders (.) ok, ui styles applied (.) ok, accessibility, serious or critical (.) ok, responsive layout on a phone (.) ok, ui primary flow (.) ok, typescript (tsc) ok, json syntax ok, scanner suppressions ok, semgrep (security errors) ok, trivy secrets ok, trivy dependency vulnerabilities (high/critical, fixable) ok, trivy misconfigurations (high/critical) ok, trivy dependency vulnerabilities (other) warn, planned files present ok, planned files fully implemented ok

review.feedback: The current implementation fails several acceptance tests and does not fully meet the listed requirements. Add placeholder tags and explicit placeholder text to founder cards, define THEME.accentText in the design tokens, and ensure all colour contrasts meet WCAG AA. Adjust the Menu button accessibility labeling, verify focus-visible styling on the CTA button, and ensure the home hero lead text contrast is sufficient. Update the Wordmark SVG styling for dark mode and render About page value descriptions. After addressing these issues, all tests should pass and requirements be satisfied.
unproven: Missing implementation of the About page placeholder tags and placeholder indication according to requirement R86 and R87. The founder cards lack visible "Placeholder" tags and explicit wording indicating content is placeholder, causing tests in __tests__/acceptance/about-render.test.ts that check for placeholder text to potentially fail.

The CSS token for accentText is not defined or used in THEME; requirement R114 expects text colours meeting WCAG AA contrast, and the contrast test in __tests__/acceptance/theme.test.ts checks THEME.accentText, which currently does not exist in src/theme/tokens.ts, causing the test to fail.

The Menu button toggle does not have an accessible label indicating "Menu" for screen readers beyond the inner span, and the button lacks aria-controls linking to the mobile nav panel with matching id; while the rendering tests check for a button with name /menu/i and proper aria-expanded, the button inner text is wrapped in <span>, but the screen reader may not see it. Ensure the button has an accessible name (e.g., aria-label) matching "Menu".

Header CTA button uses className='btn btn-primary btn-header' but does not have aria-current or proper styling for the current page active link; requirement R20 expects a "Book a consultation" button linking to /contact, which is present, but accessibility tests may check for focus-visible outlines on interactive elements; ensure the CTA button receives focus-visible style.

The Home page hero background color is set to var(--color-navy) but text color for the lead paragraph uses var(--color-muted-on-dark) which may not meet contrast ratio 4.5:1; requirement R114 expects all text colours meet WCAG AA contrast. Verify contrast for lead text.

The wordmark component does not render the SVG bell-curve mark when onDark prop is true; requirement R12 expects an inline SVG bell curve mark followed by text. The SVG is present, but the fill/stroke color does not adjust for dark backgrounds. Ensure the SVG uses var(--color-accent-light) for dark mode.
The About page values do not include descriptions in the rendered markup; requirement R88-R91 require values with titles and descriptions. Ensure the About page renders each value's description.

Implement a NotFoundPage component that displays an h1 "Page not found" and a Link to '/' (home).

Implement ContactPage with the required h1, email link, labelled form fields, validation using src/lib/contactForm, error messages, success message, and clearing of fields on successful submit.

Missing TrainingPage implementation detail: While src/pages/TrainingPage.tsx exists, its content is not shown; ensure it renders the h1 "Training", the filter buttons with proper aria-pressed handling, and course cards showing all required fields (title, audience, format, duration, learn list). Ensure the filter functionality updates the visible courses correctly.

Missing AboutPage content may be incomplete: Verify that the AboutPage fully implements the mission paragraph, Why Bayes paragraph, founder cards with placeholder tags, and values list as required. The current implementation includes these but needs to ensure the placeholder tags are clearly marked and visible for the tests.

Missing Header mobile behavior: The menu should close on Escape key press, but the current Header component adds a keydown listener only when the menu is open and closes on Escape; however, it does not return focus to the toggle or manage focus movement as required by accessibility. Add focus management to return focus to the menu button when the panel is closed via Escape.
The tagline defined as TAGLINE in src/content/site.ts is not rendered on any page, violating R7 which requires the tagline "Evidence-driven AI, built for your business." to be shown on the site.

The theme tokens for text color (mutedText) in src/theme/tokens.ts are incorrectly set to the same value as text (#2B3645) instead of a distinct muted color, and the contrast test in __tests__/acceptance/theme.test.ts expects a separate muted text color that meets WCAG AA on white. security.summary: The static marketing site’s source code is generally secure. No critical or high‑severity issues were found. A medium‑severity issue exists in the react‑router dependency (CVE‑2026‑53666, CVE‑2026‑53669) that could be exploitable only if untrusted URLs were processed, which the app does not do, but the libraries should be upgraded. Deployment hardening actions are recommended: add security headers (CSP, X‑Frame‑Options, X‑Content‑Type‑Options, Referrer‑Policy, HSTS) and serve the site over HTTPS only.

findings.issue: react-router-dom 6.30.6 contains two known CVEs (information disclosure via client‑side constructor execution and open‑redirect via backslashes). The application only uses static, hard‑coded internal routes, so the vulnerabilities are not currently exploitable, but the library version should be upgraded to a fixed release.
findings.fix: Update the dependency in package.json to a version where the CVEs are fixed (e.g., "react-router-dom": "^7.18.0") and, if necessary, adjust the code to the v7 API. Alternatively, apply any available patch that mitigates the specific CVEs.

ledger.issue: The static site does not emit HTTP security headers (Content‑Security‑Policy, X‑Frame‑Options, X‑Content‑Type‑Options, Referrer‑Policy, Strict‑Transport‑Security). Without them browsers may allow loading of unexpected resources or enable click‑jacking.
ledger.fix:
Configure the hosting/web server or CDN to send appropriate security headers. Example header values: 
- Content‑Security‑Policy: "default-src 'self'; script-src 'self'; style-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline'; img-src 'self' data:; font-src 'self';"
- X‑Frame‑Options: SAMEORIGIN
- X‑Content‑Type‑Options: nosniff
- Referrer‑Policy: no-referrer
- Strict‑Transport‑Security: max-age=31536000; includeSubDomains; preload

ui.summary: The build is in good shape. The primary flow passes in a real browser on phone and desktop, from Home to Book a consultation to field errors to success. axe reports no violations, Lighthouse accessibility is 100, and nothing overflows at 390px. Every spec'd screen was reached, including services, filtered training, about and not found. Landmarks, the skip link, the focusable <main> and per-route titles match the spec. The remaining issues are polish-level: four class names have no CSS, the footer shows content the spec doesn't call for, and one structural item (route-change focus and scroll) is not visible in Layout. Many page and CSS files were over the review budget, so the token, focus-state and form-field checks rest on the audits rather than a line-by-line read.

findings.issue: The style audit lists 'how-we-work' as an unmatched class on both viewports. The 'How we work' section has a desktop-specific layout: 4 columns with a connecting hairline. That layout almost certainly hangs off a section class, so the hairline (and possibly the 4-up grid) is likely not rendering. The section is probably falling back to a generic grid or a plain stack.
findings.fix: Add `.how-we-work` rules to global.css. At ≥1024px use a 4-column grid with a 32px gap. Draw a 1px `--color-border` hairline behind the step circles, for example with an `::before` on the list positioned at the circle's vertical center and hidden below 1024px. Or rename the class to one that is already styled.

findings.issue:
The footer adds a third paragraph, `

{TAGLINE}

`, which repeats 'Evidence-driven AI, built for your business.' The spec's footer is the wordmark, the line 'AI enablement, training and custom development.', the nav and the copyright. On Home this tagline duplicates the hero h1 word for word. The `footer-tagline` class also has no CSS (unmatched in the audit), so it renders as an unstyled paragraph in the brand column.
findings.fix: Remove the tagline paragraph (and the TAGLINE import) so the footer matches the spec. If the brand team wants it kept, add it to DESIGN.md and style `.footer-tagline` with `--color-muted-on-dark` at `--text-small`.

findings.issue: The spec requires that every navigation moves focus to <main> and scrolls to the top, or to the hash target for /services#enablement and similar links. Layout owns <main> but has no location effect. BrowserRouter scrolls to neither the top nor a hash by itself. If this logic is not in Header (not reviewable here), then two things break. Keyboard and screen-reader users stay focused on the clicked link after a route change. Pillar 'Learn more' links can land mid-page instead of on the section.
findings.fix: In Layout, add a `useLocation()` effect. On pathname or hash change: if there is a hash, call `document.getElementById(hash.slice(1))?.scrollIntoView()`, which respects the 96px scroll-margin-top. Otherwise call `window.scrollTo(0, 0)`. Then run `mainRef.current?.focus({ preventScroll: true })`. Skip the effect on the first render so initial page load focus isn't hijacked. Make sure `main:focus { outline: none }` (or a focus-visible-only rule) so a ring doesn't wrap the whole page.

findings.issue: The 'pillar-title' class is unmatched in the style audit. Pillar card h3s depend on the base h3 rule for serif 20→22px, navy and spacing. They likely lack the intended spacing between the 40px icon, title and body. 'home-page' is also unmatched, which is harmless but is dead markup.
findings.fix: Either style `.pillar-title` (`margin: var(--space-4) 0 var(--space-2)`, serif, `--text-h3`) to match the course and service card titles, or remove both class names so the markup only references classes that exist.

findings.issue: The document has no meta description and no favicon. These visitors arrive from search and referrals and are skeptical of polish. The browser tab shows a generic icon, and search results show auto-extracted text instead of the value proposition.
findings.fix: Add `<meta name="description" content="We help your team find, build and own AI that delivers measurable results, guided by two credentialed data scientists.">`. Add an inline SVG favicon of the bell-curve mark in `#1F8A8A` (`<link rel="icon" href="/favicon.svg" type="image/svg+xml">`), served locally.

findings.issue: The 'Menu' button is positioned at the top right, but the 'Book a consultation' button in the menu panel is not centered vertically or horizontally within the panel, appearing slightly misaligned.
findings.fix: Center the 'Book a consultation' button within the menu panel for better visual balance.

findings.issue: The 'Book a consultation' button in the header is slightly larger than the other nav links, which may be intentional, but it should be visually consistent with the button style used elsewhere (e.g., in the hero section).
findings.fix: Ensure the header 'Book a consultation' button matches the style and size of the hero button for visual consistency.

findings.issue: The 'Explore services' button in the hero section on desktop is visually less prominent than 'Book a consultation' — it lacks the same visual weight (e.g., no border or background color) that would make it feel like a secondary action.
findings.fix: Add a subtle visual distinction (e.g., border, background color, or hover effect) to make the 'Explore services' button feel like a clear secondary action.

findings.issue: The 'Required' labels are positioned to the right of field labels, which is unconventional and may cause confusion. Standard practice is to place required indicators next to or within the field label.
findings.fix: Move 'Required' indicators to be part of the field label text (e.g., 'Name (Required)') or place them inline with the label to the right of the field.

findings.issue: The form fields are not visually aligned with the label text above them; the labels appear slightly misaligned vertically with the input boxes.
findings.fix: Adjust vertical alignment so labels sit directly above their respective input fields with consistent spacing.

findings.issue: The form card is not fully aligned with the left edge of the content area; there's a small gap on the left, which breaks the visual flow.
findings.fix: Adjust the form card's left margin to align flush with the content area's left edge for a more cohesive desktop layout.

findings.issue: The form fields are too close to the top of the screen, leaving insufficient padding above the first field and below the header, making it feel cramped.
findings.fix: Add padding above the form to create breathing room and align it with the top of the viewport.

findings.issue: The 'Required' labels are placed inside rounded badges, which are visually inconsistent with the form field styling and may not be accessible to all users.
findings.fix: Move 'Required' labels to the right of the field label, or use a consistent visual indicator like an asterisk with a tooltip.

findings.issue: The form is not aligned to a grid; fields are left-aligned but not consistently spaced, creating an unbalanced layout.
findings.fix: Apply a consistent grid system to align fields and spacing for improved visual harmony.

findings.issue: The form is positioned too far right, leaving a large empty space on the left. The desktop layout doesn’t use the full width or leverage the available space effectively.
findings.fix: Center or left-align the form with appropriate padding to utilize the desktop viewport more efficiently.

findings.issue: The form field borders are inconsistent: Name has a teal border, Email has a red border, and Company has a grey border. This creates visual noise and doesn't clearly indicate error states for all fields.
findings.fix: Standardize border colors: use red for errors, grey for non-errors, and teal for success states or focus.

findings.issue: The error messages are positioned directly below the fields but not aligned with the field labels, creating visual misalignment.
findings.fix: Align error messages with the field labels and ensure consistent vertical spacing.

findings.issue: The 'What can we help with?' dropdown is positioned too low, creating an awkward gap before the 'Message' field.
findings.fix: Adjust vertical spacing to create a more balanced and compact form layout.

findings.issue: visual quality 7/10 on 'contact form with errors' (target 8+, minimum 7): The contact form is clean and functional, with clear visual hierarchy and error states. However, it lacks polish in typography, spacing, and form design, and the desktop layout feels underutilized. It’s good but not exceptional.
findings.fix: Address this screen's findings until it looks polished and professional.

findings.issue: The 'Required' badges are small and may be hard to read on smaller screens; consider increasing size or using bold weight for better visibility.
findings.fix: Increase the font size or weight of the 'Required' badges to ensure they are easily readable on phone screens.

findings.issue: The form fields are not fully optimized for touch; the input fields could benefit from increased tap targets and padding for better usability.
findings.fix: Add padding and increase the height of input fields to ensure they are easier to tap on mobile devices.

findings.issue: The form is left-aligned and lacks horizontal padding on the right side, which could feel cramped on wider desktop screens.
findings.fix: Add padding to the right of the form to balance the layout and improve visual breathing room on desktop.

findings.issue: The 'What can we help with?' dropdown does not have a clear visual indicator of its state (e.g., no chevron or highlight when selected).
findings.fix: Add a subtle visual indicator (like a chevron or border change) to show the dropdown's selected state.

findings.issue: The 'Required' labels are slightly misaligned with their respective input fields, creating inconsistent vertical spacing.
findings.fix: Adjust the vertical alignment of the 'Required' labels to align consistently with the top of their input fields.

findings.issue: The 'What can we help with?' dropdown is slightly misaligned with the 'Message' field below it, creating inconsistent vertical spacing.
findings.fix: Adjust the vertical spacing between the dropdown and the 'Message' field to match the spacing above.

findings.issue: The 'Menu' button is positioned at the top right, but the navigation panel doesn't appear to be visible in the screenshot, making it unclear how the navigation is accessed on mobile.
findings.fix: Ensure the menu panel is visible when the menu button is pressed, and confirm it slides down with clear visual feedback.

findings.issue: The 'About' section heading is not styled with the same weight or size as the 'Why Bayes' heading, breaking visual hierarchy.
findings.fix: Apply consistent heading styles across all section titles to reinforce visual hierarchy.

findings.issue: The desktop layout has excessive white space at the bottom, leaving large empty areas below 'Founders' section.
findings.fix: Add content or a visual anchor (like a CTA or footer) to fill the unused space and improve visual completeness.

findings.issue: The 'Founders' section is cut off at the bottom of the screen, suggesting content is truncated or not fully rendered.
findings.fix: Ensure the 'Founders' section is fully visible in both viewport sizes, or add a scroll indicator if content exceeds viewport.

findings.issue: visual quality 7/10 on 'about' (target 8+, minimum 7): The About page is visually clean and well-structured, with consistent typography and spacing. It effectively uses hierarchy and alignment, and the primary action is clearly visible. However, it lacks visual polish in key areas like form design and empty states, and the desktop layout feels underutilized.
findings.fix: Address this screen's findings until it looks polished and professional.

findings.issue: The 'Back to home' button is slightly narrower than the 'View services' link, creating a small visual imbalance.
findings.fix: Adjust the button width to match the link's width for visual consistency.

findings.issue: The 'View services' link is positioned slightly lower than the button, creating a minor vertical misalignment.
findings.fix: Align the link with the top of the button for a cleaner visual hierarchy.
